title: Ahead-of-time compiled code atoms
preamble:
# Ahead-of-time compiled code atoms

The ahead-of-time (AOT) compiled code atom (`CompiledCode`): the `CompiledCode` atom
format, the body layout (slot table + machine code), architecture
strings, loader behaviour, and the fallback chain when no blob
matches.

**What is emitted, and how it is built, is not here.** The C
function signatures and calling convention, the compilation
pipeline, the flag model and the ESP32-S3 XIP arrangement are
[IAOT], because this document must not assume the emission
target is C — an implementation targeting the BEAM would generate
Erlang and need an Erlang calling convention ([STYL.2.13.6]).

Prefix `RAOT`.

Paired with:
- [RDSC] — container format and
  unknown-atom skip policy (RDSC.9.4).
- [RLOW] — the Rete network the AOT pipeline
  compiles from, and which the runtime interprets when no `CompiledCode` atom
  matches the current architecture (RAOT.1.1). The fallback is
  two-level: `CompiledCode`, then interpreted.
- `proto/aot.proto` — proto3 definition for the `CompiledCode` atom body.
- [RCLI] — the `--emit-aot` and
  `--emit-rete` flags that request `CompiledCode` blobs.

## What this is not

- Not a general JIT spec.  The code is compiled ahead of time by the
  DSC compiler, not at engine startup or rule-fire time.
- Not a specification of the C code the pipeline generates.  That is
  a compiler-implementation concern; this doc specifies the interface
  the generated code must satisfy.
- Not a language or expression spec.  The expression surface is
  defined by [LEXP].
